newsitem.title: GERMANY: Duesseldorf airport has DM107.7 mln loss due fire.
newsitem.headline: Duesseldorf airport has DM107.7 mln loss due fire.

text.p: The April 1996 fire at Duesseldorf airport led to losses of 107.7 million marks in 1996 for the airport operating company compared to profit of 36 million marks the previous year, the group said on Tuesday.

Sales in 1996 fell by 37 million marks to 494 million marks after the fire, in which 17 people died and 58 were injured, seriously disrupted operations at the airport, which is one of Germany's main regional airports.
Matthias Teumpel, managing director of Flughafen Duesseldorf, said the group expected 1997 turnover of over 500 million marks and for earnings to reach break-even.
Teumpel said that getting the airport operational again after the fire involved extra costs of 40 million marks, which was spent on emergency tents, new installations or extra shuttle bus facilities.
The construction of temporary facilities and the renovation of the affected airport areas required a further investment of 154 million marks.
The group also set aside reserves of 163 million marks for possible recourse claims from insurers and victims.
